boundary_rationale: A first-person night episode opens on the feminine-marked perfect אֲנִ֥י יְשֵׁנָ֖ה (oshb:Song.5.2, byte tier) 'I was asleep', WEB's “I was asleep, but my heart was awake.” (web:Song.5.2) standing as corroboration rather than the ground; it runs through the search and the watchmen's beating to its close in the adjuration variant הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּנ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם (oshb:Song.5.8, byte tier) 'I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem', continuing אִֽם תִּמְצְאוּ֙ (oshb:Song.5.8, byte tier) 'if you find' — the im-timtze'u/mah-tagidu shape that lacks the gazelle-and-doe pairing carried by the fuller formula elsewhere. The immediately preceding verse (web:Song.5.1) closes under a setumah division, so the episode opens on a fresh section by the WLC layout as well as by the switch from summons to first-person narration.

device_notes: Formula-variation discipline: this is the im-timtze'u/mah-tagidu shape, distinct in shape from the full daughters-plus-gazelles form and from the mah-ta'iru variant later in the part (both held elsewhere) — three attested shapes, never harmonized. Two byte-true devices straddle this row's own seams, disclosed rather than left implicit: at the front seam, the man's address vocabulary פִּתְחִי לִ֞י אֲחֹתִ֤י רַעְיָתִי֙ (oshb:Song.5.2, byte tier) continues the bride-epithet chain from oshb:Song.4.9, 4.10, 4.12 and 5.1, but it stands INSIDE the man's quoted call framed by her own narration rather than as address continuing across the seam in her own voice; at the back seam, הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) repeats the oath root immediately across this row's own closing verse, the daughters quoting it back — the same-root site the four-site adjuration count excludes on speech-role grounds.

boundary_rationale: His renewed praise of her opens on the vocative יָפָ֨ה אַ֤תְּ רַעְיָתִי֙ (oshb:Song.6.4, byte tier) 'beautiful are you, my love', using rayati (his word for her) with the 2fs pronoun, and runs through body-part imagery carrying genuine 2fs address forms — עֵינַ֨יִךְ֙ and שַׂעְרֵךְ֙ (oshb:Song.6.5, byte tier) at MT 6:5, שִׁנַּ֨יִךְ֙ (oshb:Song.6.6, byte tier) at MT 6:6, רַקָּתֵ֔ךְ מִבַּ֖עַד לְצַמָּתֵֽךְ at MT 6:7 (oshb:Song.6.7, byte tier) — into a numeric comparison against the royal household at MT 6:8, which carries no address form, and her uniqueness declaration אַחַ֥ת הִיא֙ יוֹנָתִ֣י תַמָּתִ֔י (oshb:Song.6.9, byte tier) 'she is one, my dove, my perfect one'. MT 6:9 turns to third-feminine-singular predication carrying 1cs-possessive epithets rather than continuing the 2fs address, and no address form stands at MT 6:8 or MT 6:9 either. The span closes on the marveling exclamation מִי זֹ֥את הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה כְּמוֹ שָׁ֑חַר (oshb:Song.6.10, byte tier) 'who is this who looks out like the dawn', itself carrying no address form, and closing on אֲיֻמָּ֖ה כַּנִּדְגָּלֽוֹת (oshb:Song.6.10, byte tier) — the identical byte-tier phrase that closes the span's own opening verse, אֲיֻמָּ֖ה כַּנִּדְגָּלֽוֹת (oshb:Song.6.4, byte tier) (byte sweep: 2 verses, MT 6:4 and MT 6:10), a refrain bracket closing the unit it opened. WEB: “You are beautiful, my love, as Tirzah, lovely as Jerusalem, awesome as an army with banners.” (web:Song.6.4); “Who is she who looks out as the morning, beautiful as the moon, clear as the sun, and awesome as an army with banners?” (web:Song.6.10). A second recurrence runs alongside the bracket at accent_stripped tier only: בָּרָ֥ה (oshb:Song.6.9) and בָּרָה֙ (oshb:Song.6.10) match once cantillation is stripped, corroborating continuity across the seam without driving the close. No 2fs address form and no gendered-form change stands anywhere across MT 6:8-6:10, so nothing there licenses a cut; the byte-tier inclusio is what closes the unit at MT 6:10. MT 6:9 sits under its own setumah, span-internal, and MT 6:10 closes under a further setumah at the span's back edge, both single-witness and disclosed as corroboration only.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending the span at MT 6:9 and reading MT 6:10 as the opening verse of a fresh unit was the leading rejected alternative: MT 6:10 carries the bare mi-zot interrogative (skeleton sweep: 3 verses, MT 3:6, 6:10, 8:5) but no ascent verb, so it is not a member of the ascent-run formula מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר (oshb:Song.8.5, skeleton sweep: 2 verses, MT 3:6 and MT 8:5), and an opener reading resting on that blended object is rejected in favor of the byte-tier inclusio that closes the unit at MT 6:10 instead. The internal MT 6:7|6:8 join inside the span carries no marked seam either, which the row's confidence reflects rather than resolves.

boundary_rationale: The seam verse (web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1) opens a new exchange against its own front seam: oshb:Song.6.12 closes in first-person singular — לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי נַפְשִׁ֣י שָׂמַ֔תְנִי (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) — while oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13 opens with the repeated 2fs imperative summons שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֨וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית שׁ֥וּבִי שׁ֖וּבִי (byte tier) 'return, return, the Shulammite; return, return', addressed to an epithet unique to this verse (הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית — byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide, 2 occurrences in-verse), an addressee-and-person shift of tier-1 class. The catchword נָדִֽיב (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) immediately before and בַּת נָדִ֑יב (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, byte tier) immediately after bracket this single-verse span on both seams (skeleton sweep: 2 verses book-wide). Within the verse the summons is followed by מַֽה תֶּחֱזוּ֙ בַּשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) 'why do you gaze at the Shulammite' — WEB “Return, return, Shulammite! Return, return, that we may gaze at you. Why do you desire to gaze at the Shulammite, as at the dance of Mahanaim?” (web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1). Whether the second half is spoken by the same voice as the opening summons is argued from the bytes alone (not from the WEB [SPEAKER] heading), so the call-and-question is held as one exchange rather than split at an unmarked internal line.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row forward into web:Song.7.1 = oshb:Song.7.2's wasf opening was rejected: the imperative summons and its dance-of-Mahanaim question form a closed rhetorical unit distinct in form from the body-part praise that begins the next verse.

boundary_rationale: The book's final call-and-response: חֲבֵרִ֛ים מַקְשִׁיבִ֥ים לְקוֹלֵ֖ךְ הַשְׁמִיעִֽינִי (oshb:Song.8.13, byte tier) 'companions listening for your voice, let me hear it' — מַקְשִׁיבִ֥ים a masculine-plural participle agreeing with חֲבֵרִ֛ים, and only the closing הַשְׁמִיעִֽינִי a feminine-singular imperative — WEB “You who dwell in the gardens, with friends in attendance, let me hear your voice!” (web:Song.8.13), answered by her closing summons בְּרַ֣ח דּוֹדִ֗י (oshb:Song.8.14, byte tier) 'flee, my beloved', WEB “Come away, my beloved! Be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices!” (web:Song.8.14). The pair is held together not because the gender markers are thin but because they are MT 8:13's and MT 8:14's cleanest 2fs/2ms minimal pair set against each other across the row's own internal seam — לְקוֹלֵ֖ךְ (oshb:Song.8.13, byte tier), final kaf plus sheva, the 2fs shape, against לְךָ֤ (oshb:Song.8.14, byte tier), final kaf plus qamats, the 2ms shape — alongside the vocative הַיוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת in 8:13, the masculine-singular imperatives בְּרַ֣ח and וּֽדְמֵה in 8:14, and the explicit vocative דּוֹדִ֗י (byte tier), one of the book's 24 attested-exact-spelling dodi sites (sweep: 24 verses) — so the two-verse exchange is held together as one answered dialogue on the strength of these gender-marked and vocative markers, not despite their thinness.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the book's close into two single-verse rows (his call, her answer) was considered, but the 2fs/2ms minimal pair and the vocative דּוֹדִ֗י (oshb:Song.8.14) together argue the two verses as one answered exchange rather than two independent turns.
